metadata.description: Curated, source-verified knowledge base of the Python quantitative-finance library ecosystem, packaged as Agent Skills.

plugins.name: fin-core
plugins.description: US/global quant stack: finding and resolving identifiers, market data sourcing and engineering, SEC/macro point-in-time data, backtesting engines, broker APIs, signals, factors, portfolio construction, risk analytics, backtest validation, derivatives pricing — plus the research-integrity guards that keep a backtest honest. 21 skills, measured at ~4,557 tokens of skill-listing budget: one past the ~20 at which Claude Code starts silently dropping descriptions to name-only, so that last increment of breadth is a deliberate, OPT-IN cost. Set skillListingBudgetFraction to 0.03 before installing anything alongside it.

plugins.name: fin-china
plugins.description: China A-share / Greater China quant stack: akshare, tushare, baostock, efinance, adata, mootdx, jqdatasdk, rqdatac, Wind, plus vnpy / qlib / RQAlpha / tqsdk and the A-share-specific traps (qfq look-ahead, T+1, price limits, suspension, 公告日 vs 报告期).

plugins.name: fin-asia
plugins.description: Asia-Pacific ex-mainland-China: Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan, Korea, India, Singapore and Australia — futu-api, tigeropen, shioaji, FinMind, J-Quants, pykrx, FinanceDataReader, kiteconnect and the date-keyed regime changes (Korea's short-selling bans, India's T+1/SEBI overhaul, the 2022 TSE restructuring) that silently break backtests.

plugins.name: fin-futures-fx
plugins.description: Futures and FX: continuous-contract construction (difference vs ratio vs unadjusted and when each is wrong), roll rules as researcher degrees of freedom, contract specs and margin, CME session structure, plus FX quote conventions, pip sizing and carry — the parts an equity-shaped toolchain silently gets wrong.

plugins.name: fin-crypto
plugins.description: Crypto market data and execution: ccxt, cryptofeed, python-binance, freqtrade, jesse, hummingbot — and the 24/7-market assumptions that break equity-derived tooling.

plugins.name: fin-llm
plugins.description: LLM- and ML-for-finance: agent frameworks (TradingAgents, FinRobot, RD-Agent, FinGPT), reinforcement learning and deep learning for trading, finance MCP servers, and the published evidence on whether any of it survives lookahead leakage, transaction costs, and multiple-testing correction.

plugins.name: fin-libraries
plugins.description: One skill per library - fine-grained retrieval for 24 of the most-used Python quant packages, each leading with the single default or bug that silently produces wrong numbers. OPT-IN AND EXPENSIVE: measured at ~5,298 tokens of skill-listing budget on its own, and 24 skills already exceeds the ~20 at which Claude Code starts silently dropping descriptions to name-only. Set skillListingBudgetFraction to 0.03 before installing it, 0.05 to run it alongside fin-core, and 0.06 for every plugin.

plugins.name: fin-models
plugins.description: Quantitative model families - factor models, covariance and risk models, VaR/CVaR and their backtests, portfolio optimizers, volatility models, state-space and Kalman, cointegration and statistical arbitrage, time-series forecasting, option pricing and implied-volatility surfaces, term-structure and credit models. One skill per model family: which Python implementation is verified, the pitfalls that produce wrong numbers, and an executable script that reproduces the claim.

plugins.name: fin-strategies
plugins.description: Strategy and execution algorithms - trend following and time-series momentum, alpha combination and neutralization, execution algorithms (VWAP, TWAP, POV, Almgren-Chriss), market-making models, position sizing and Kelly. One skill per family, source-verified, each with an executable script and the traps that flatter a backtest.

plugins.name: fin-ml
plugins.description: Machine learning on financial data without the leaks that make it look like it works - fractional differentiation, triple-barrier labels, meta-labeling, sample weights for overlapping outcomes, feature importance that survives correlated features, bet sizing, and structural-break tests. One skill per technique, source-verified, each with an executable script and the measured size of the trap it prevents.

plugins.name: fin-microstructure
plugins.description: Order-book and high-frequency models, dependence, and simulation - limit-order-book queue models, Hawkes processes for order arrivals, copulas and tail dependence, and Monte Carlo methods including variance reduction and Longstaff-Schwartz for American options. One skill per family, source-verified, each with an executable script and the trap that produces a wrong number.

plugins.name: fin-macro
plugins.description: Macro data as a point-in-time object - real-time vintages versus today's revised series, release calendars and embargo times, seasonal adjustment as a second silent vintage, recession indicators that are assigned retrospectively, nowcasting with dynamic factor models, and the non-US central-bank APIs. One skill per topic, source-verified, each with an executable script and the measured size of the trap it prevents.

plugins.name: fin-tax-accounting
plugins.description: The after-tax P&L a pre-tax backtest never shows - tax lot matching and cost basis, wash sales, Section 1256 sixty-forty treatment for futures and index options, crypto per-wallet basis after Rev. Proc. 2024-28, A-share stamp duty and holding-period dividend tax, and dividend withholding against gross index benchmarks. One skill per rule, each dated, each with an executable script. Modelling assumptions, not tax advice.

plugins.name: fin-fixed-income
plugins.description: Bonds, rates and the conventions every other fixed-income number sits on - day counts and accrued interest, gilt ex-dividend windows and negative accrued, yield measures and bill discount quotes, duration convexity and DV01, SOFR compounded in arrears, LIBOR fallbacks under Regulation ZZ, and OIS multi-curve discounting. One skill per topic, each with an executable script and a measured trap.

plugins.name: fin-credit
plugins.description: Credit spreads, CDS mechanics and ratings migration - Z-spread against I-spread against G-spread and OAS and when they diverge, the ISDA standard model and points upfront, what TRACE actually reports and what its dissemination caps censor, and ratings migration matrices and the embedding problem that puts negative probabilities in a six-month root. Four skills, each with an executable script and a measured trap. CDS indices and tranches, default and recovery data, and portfolio loss models are planned and not here yet.

plugins.name: trading-skills
plugins.description: FEDERATED - the claims inside are not verified by this repo. agiprolabs' 68 skills: Solana execution (RPC, Jito bundles, pump.fun), DeFi analytics (DefiLlama, DexScreener, Birdeye), MEV, wallet profiling, prediction markets, and tax lots (cost basis, wash-sale detection, harvesting). About 3x the default listing budget, and ~20 skills overlap fin-core topics - its vectorbt skill does not mention the same-bar-fill default that lib-vectorbt leads with. Installs disabled; enable after reading its README.
